title: page of wands: potentiality of beginnings
content:
from tarot work diaries — using the tarot as an intuitive guide for creative business. currently pulling one card a week to guide my process.

the Page of Wands channels the energy of following inspiration, starting small creative fires, and playing with beginnings — or, at least, wielding the beginner’s mindset when approaching familiar things.

this page from the Rider–Waite deck is dressed in yellow robes with a feather in their hat, and is about to embark on a desert adventure. they bring along a magic staff — like a wand, sprouting with life and possibility — and a standing posture of ease, confidence, and curiosity.

okay, all great. but what if I’m not really feeling this?

the opposite of this card

the week I pulled the Page of Wands as my guiding card, my body felt like a swamp, and my energy felt like sisyphus pushing boulders up a hill. I was in the middle of a client deployment project that was its own leviathan-hydra, and I counted twelve different other ongoing pieces — from drafts of unfinished writings, to podcast episodes, to launching a new business website — that were all clogging my system.

I had also just gotten my period, and on most days, I walked around feeling on edge, with the beginnings of a headache. instead of feeling light and prancing in the desert to start something new, I felt overwhelmed, stale, and soggy. I wanted to get things out of my system, but I felt time and energy scarcity. and here, the page of wands showed up — inviting me to consider the energy of beginnings.

beginnings as small fires

the thing about beginnings is this: they’re energizing, and a great way to procrastinate. my Aries moon delights in starting small fires, and once it’s a bit bored, it’ll wander off, forget about / abandon the fires, and eventually start a new one.

beginnings live in the space of infinite possibility — like a child talking about its dreams. there’s no pressure to “grow up” or “be responsible” or “make it happen.” we leave that work to adults. the Page of Wands is like this — always eager to use their magic wand (aka, creative energy) to play with something new — without wanting to get bogged down in its follow through and execution. it leaves a gazillion projects as open loops, and then wanders off to the next thing.

(meanwhile, those open loops stay open — and pile up, and one day, you wake up feeling like a traffic jam / swamp).


completion frees energy to play

when I drew this card for my week, I didn’t interpret it as an invitation to start another thing — I clearly didn’t have energy for that.

instead, I saw how the Page of Wands' inability to follow-through was the energy that led me here, in the first place. I asked myself how I could embody its energy even while feeling stuck in a slow, sluggish state.

  • how can the Page of Wands guide completion, release, and endings?

  • how can I approach completion in a playful, creative way?

  • what do I need to access the Page of Wands lightness again?


in my case, this meant doing things

  1. making a map of all the projects that needed “clearing” — in order to make space for new things to emerge

  2. not forcing myself down a check box to-do list, but listening to what the creative urge within me wanted to do, and then gently guiding my attention to that work

  3. allowing deep integration work (journaling, tarot, writing, reflection time, systems) — as a way of cleansing and processing

after I was patient with myself through a week of feeling heavy, very un-Page of Wands energy, I woke up on Sunday suddenly brimming with a hundred ideas and sparks of inspiration. it was as if even while I was doing tedious work, the Page of Wands lived just underneath the surface, waiting for its time to surface. I hadn’t finished everything, but I did allowed myself to make a little more space.

cycles of creative completion are never linear. you release some things, and new things emerge.

part of the practice, then, is sensing and trusting that Page of Wands energy IS always there, ready to guide you on a new creative adventure. you could think of it like a creative spirit-friend — knocking on your window with a wink, but willing to wait patiently outside, entertaining itself — while you finish your homework.

contemplation questions

  • what are you feeling inspired by? what new adventures or urges are calling to you?

  • what is your relationship to beginnings?

  • what if you gave yourself permission to play, explore, and experiment? how would you work differently?

  • if you’re feeling heavy or unmotivated, what do you need to do in order to create more space to play?
